To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum stable operational current density of a superconductor subjected a linear thermal disturbance is determined by the thermal disturbance rate, the wire diameter, and the operational current density, and that the maximum current density that can be recovered after quenching depends on the wire diameter and the operational current.
a superconducting wire or a superconducting cylinder subjected to an instantaneous thermal disturbance will be quenched if the instability parameter is greater than unity.

the stability of the wire/cylinder-type superconductor is strongly affected by the diameter of the wire/cylinders and the operational current density, and that the wire/cylinder-type superconductor with smaller diameter or higher operational current density is more susceptible to quenching and less likely to recover from the quenching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of superconductivity in a wire or cylinder subjected to a thermal disturbance.
the quenching and recovering of the superconductivity for superconducting wire and cylinder.
the stability of the operation of superconducting wires subjected to a thermal disturbance, and the mechanism of loss and restoration of superconductivity in the wires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cylinder/wire-type conductor is more stable than the tape/film-type conductor under thermal disturbance.
a wire-type superconductor is more stable than the tape/film-type under the same operational conditions.
the cylinder/wire-type conductor has a lower critical current density than the tape/film-type conductor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a superconducting wire or a cylinder can be operated at higher currents than a superconducting tape or a film if the thermal conductivity is not too small.
we developed a method for the analysis of quenching of superconductor wires and cylinders.
the stability of a cylinder/wired-type superconductor depends on the ratio of convective cooling rate to Joule heating rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for wire-type superconductors, the critical current density for stable operation is much higher than for tape/film type superconductors.
a wire-type superconductor is more stable against thermal disturbances than a tape/film-type one.
the stability criterion for wire-type superconductor is more stringent than that for tape/film superconductor.
